data.name: Barzah
data.gender_notes: Barzah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A woman who cultivates and tends to a garden, nurturing it with care and love until it blooms into beauty. The name Barzah is derived from the Arabic word 'barzaj' meaning 'gardener'. It is a beautiful and meaningful name for a baby girl, signifying growth, beauty, and nurturing. The name Barzah carries the meaning “Gardener, Sower of seeds” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Barzah usually hope their child will grow to embody gardener, sower of seeds and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the nurturing and care given by Allah (God) to His creation, reminding us to do the same for those around us.
data.etymology: Barzah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gardener, Sower of seeds.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Barzah total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

The cultivation and care of gardens have long been a source of pride and joy for many Islamic communities. The name symbolizes the idea of hard work, patience, and dedication as one tends to the land and watches it transform into a beautiful and fruitful garden.
data.spiritual_significance: Barzah is also a deeply spiritual name, representing the idea of nurturing and caring for creation as a manifestation of God's love and guidance. In Islamic tradition, it is believed that Allah (God) has created the world as a garden, and we are caretakers of this garden. The name Barzah is a reminder of our role as stewards of creation, and the importance of tending to our spiritual gardens, just as we tend to a physical garden. It is a name that inspires us to be mindful of our actions and to cultivate a beautiful and fruitful spiritual life, just as Barzah tends to her garden with care and love.
